versioning: patch release: one opt-in submit option (--smt); no schema change (bit 2 of jobs.exclusive_timing), no node configuration key, no new scheduling input, no new side effect

database_schema.change: none; --smt is stored as exclusive_timing 3 (bit 1 exclusive timing, bit 2 SMT); rollback leaves the schema at 10 and 0.8.1 reads such a job as an --exclusive-timing job

node_config: the install keeps the live node.json byte for byte (0.8.2 adds no key); config/zenobia-16core-node.json is 0.8.1's plus a note and differs from the live file only in borrow.lend_siblings (set true by hand on 2026-11-06)
request: approved by Trevor on 2026-11-07 (about 13:00 Mountain Time) for the i-PULSE logo run: MOOSE/Zapdos with 16 MPI ranks and --n-threads=2, assembly 64% of runtime; design from simqueue-0.8.2-20261106/HANDOFF.txt (paused 2026-11-06 after 'MT' was misread as multithreading)
problem: 0.8.1 sets a job unit's CPUAffinity to its allocated cores only (a 16-core job: 0-15); their SMT siblings (16-31) stay idle; --exclusive-timing keeps them unlent but does not give them to the job

design.option: simq submit/run --smt (owner jobs): unit CPUAffinity = the allocated cores and their SMT siblings that no partition allocates (NodeConfig.smt_affinity); the allocation, the planner, the lease files and SIMQ_CPU_LIST stay the physical cores
design.environment: SIMQ_SMT=1, SIMQ_THREADS_PER_CORE (the fewest logical CPUs of any of the job's cores: 2 on zenobia), SIMQ_CPU_LIST_SMT (the whole affinity, e.g. 0-31); only for --smt jobs
design.storage: jobs.exclusive_timing as a bit field: 1 = exclusive timing, 2 = SMT; --smt stores 3, so every reader that takes the column as a truth value (scheduler Request, borrow.py, telemetry.py, 0.8.1) protects an --smt job's cores and siblings as an exclusive-timing job's
design.protection: an --smt job is an --exclusive-timing job: its cores and siblings are never lent (also with borrow.lend_siblings true), a starting one preempts borrowers on its siblings; owner jobs are never placed on siblings
design.wrapper: jobwrap.py checks sched_getaffinity against the spec's affinity_cpu_list (--smt jobs only; others against cpu_list as before) and logs an SMT: line
design.display: simq show: request 'smt: cores with their SMT siblings, exclusive timing', an SMT line with the unit's affinity and threads per core, CPU time can exceed 100% of the cores; simq doctor: 'SMT jobs' line; submit --json: smt true; --test-only: cpu_list_smt, threads_per_core
design.refused: --smt with --borrow; --smt on cores without a free SMT sibling
design.cpu_utilization: unchanged definition (CPU time / runtime x allocated cores): an --smt job can reach about 2.0
design.rollback: 0.8.1 runs a queued --smt job as an exclusive-timing job on its cores only; a running one keeps its affinity under the 0.8.2 jobwrap.py until it ends
design.rejected_alternative: an additive smt column (schema 11) would make the release 0.9.0 by the versioning rule and need a schema downgrade on rollback
design.mpi: use moose-mpiexec --bind-to none (ranks inherit the unit's affinity); Open MPI 5's --map-by core --bind-to core maps over the machine's cores from core 0 and ignores the job's affinity (validation: a job on cores 2-3 got ranks on 0,16 and 1,17), so it is right only for a job holding every core; not new in 0.8.2 and true without --smt too

unchanged_for_jobs_without_smt: same unit command (CPUAffinity, properties, setenv), same spec keys and values, same job environment, same log, exclusive_timing 0 or 1 as before: test_smt.StartPathTests compares 0.8.1 and 0.8.2 for a plain, an --exclusive-timing and a GPU job
features: simq submit/run --smt: CPU affinity = the job's cores and their SMT siblings, 2 threads per core on zenobia
--smt jobs protected as --exclusive-timing jobs (no lending of cores or siblings)
simq show SMT line, simq doctor 'SMT jobs' line, submit --json smt, --test-only cpu_list_smt
